named_confounds: very small early-period cells (e.g., romance n=40 with zero hits, collection n=37)
imprecise dating (54% of works low/medium date confidence; most years decade-coded)
corpus sampling heavily skewed to post-1876 works
rationale: Methods: 6,766 works, one passage each (n_passages=1), so the work rate is 0/1 for DISTANCE_TRAVEL. Split at year>=1876. I took the late-minus-early difference in mean rate within each of the 8 genres, then averaged the genres equally. Point estimate +0.025 passage-rate units. A bootstrap stratified by genre and period gives a 95% CI of [0.004, 0.046]. An author-clustered bootstrap gives [0.0001, 0.049], which barely excludes zero. Coverage: only 931 works are early versus 5,835 late, and several early genre cells are tiny. Romance (40 early works, 0 hits) and collection (37 early works) supply much of the effect. Adventure and sensation_mystery go down slightly. Robustness: the estimate shrinks to +0.015 for high-date-confidence works only, +0.013 within a 1856-1895 window, and +0.020 without the other/collection genres. It is +0.032 for single-edition works. Decade means rise unevenly (1870s 0.059, 1860s 0.105). Alternative explanations: changes in genre and author mix, sparse early sampling, dating error near the cutoff, and annotation drift could each produce a small difference like this. Passage IDs only show that travel/distance appears as a theme; they cannot establish a trend. The direction leans toward an increase, but its size is small and it is not robust across clustering and sensitivity checks, so I abstain.
